# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (Sponsor)
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has three AI use cases, each at a different stage:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers identified are the EU AI Act and GDPR.

In June 2026 an internal audit finding recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Client operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. It intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although that start date is not yet fixed.

Three stated constraints shape this proposal:

- The approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement would deliver a governance document set written by outsiders. The Client would then have to adopt, staff and operate that document set without having built it. The Guided AI GRC Build works differently. The Client's own team builds the system through weekly workshops, coaching and structured asynchronous work. As a result, the Client retains the knowledge and can operate the system after Week 12.

Three features of the Client's situation favour this approach:

1. **The audit finding concerns operations as much as documentation.** An inventory stays accurate only when the people closest to each system maintain it. A guided build establishes that maintenance habit during the program rather than leaving it as a post-delivery task.
2. **The Client already runs two management systems.** An AIMS that sits apart from the ISMS and the QMS would create parallel structures to maintain. The build is designed to attach AI governance to existing artifacts wherever those artifacts are confirmed.
3. **Production readiness requires owners who have rehearsed the process.** Governance in place before visual inspection reaches production means people at the Client who have already run the processes, not a document set waiting to be adopted.

The program works from two open frameworks:

- the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-level material draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

Three principles guide every session: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

The ISO/IEC 42001 column shows the readiness themes each week supports. This proposal does not promise certification or any audit outcome.

| Week | Spine | Tamarack Instruments tailoring | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Draft AIMS charter; assign system owners; confirm the second production workflow (see Section 4); agree on the internal auditors' role; executive steering | Context, leadership, roles |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Inventory the three named systems in priority order (see below); run a discovery sweep for further systems | Context, AI system records |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | Classify each system against the EU AI Act; build a risk scale compatible with existing ISMS and QMS scales where confirmed | Planning, risk criteria |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Full assessments for the chatbot and visual inspection; a lighter pre-assessment for sales forecasting | AI risk assessment, AI system impact assessment |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Operating AI risk register; treatment plans with owners | Risk treatment |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set drafted for adoption; mid-point steering | Leadership, AI policy |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates covering pilot to production for visual inspection | Operation, lifecycle |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier review for any third-party AI components; evidence collection starts | Third-party relationships, documented information |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Human oversight design for the two production workflows | Operation, use of AI systems |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring metrics and review cadence for each workflow | Performance evaluation |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change routes; first evidence review | Improvement, nonconformity |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Evidence walkthrough; readiness gap list; closing steering | Internal audit readiness, management review |

**Inventory priority (Week 2):**

1. **Customer service chatbot.** This is the only deployed system, so it is the Client's current live exposure. Under the EU AI Act, transparency obligations for systems that interact with people are a likely consideration (confirm with external counsel). Whether the chatbot processes customer data, and where, is currently Unknown and will be captured in Week 2 against the EU data residency constraint.
2. **AI visual inspection.** This system is tied directly to your Q2 2027 objective. Whether it touches production staff is Unknown. If it does, works council consultation must come first, as the stated constraint requires (confirm with external counsel).
3. **AI sales forecasting.** This system is entered as a planned record so that it comes under governance at the design stage rather than after deployment.

Any further AI systems in use are Unknown and will be surfaced by the Week 2 discovery sweep.

**Integration with incumbent frameworks.** The Profile Block names the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 QMS. It does not identify the specific artifacts the AIMS would attach to, such as a risk register, document control procedure, supplier process or incident process. Each weekly integration point is therefore recorded as Unknown until the Client confirms the relevant artifact in Week 1. The aim is to extend existing artifacts rather than duplicate them.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS comprising all six of the following elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**One decision is needed before mobilization.** Element 5 requires two workflows in production use by Week 12, but the Profile Block identifies only one deployed system, the chatbot. Visual inspection is targeted for production in Q2 2027, and whether it will be in production use by Week 12 is Unknown. The second workflow must therefore be identified and confirmed in Week 1. Possible routes include a further production AI use surfaced by the inventory sweep or a confirmed visual inspection go-live date that falls before Week 12. Whichever candidate is chosen, the program will not advance a production change to meet this element if it would bypass works council consultation.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

All figures below are **estimates**. They cover the weekly workshop (about two hours), the coaching session (about one hour) and asynchronous work. Actual effort will be tracked from Week 1.

| Role | Typical week (estimate) | Peak weeks and focus (estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 hours | W1, W3, W6, W12: 5 to 6 hours (charter, EU AI Act classification, policy adoption, steering) |
| CISO | 4 to 5 hours | W2, W8, W11: 6 to 7 hours (inventory, suppliers, incident response) |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 5 hours | W3, W7, W11: 6 to 7 hours (risk methodology, lifecycle, change management) |
| Head of Data | 4 to 5 hours | W2, W4, W10: 6 to 7 hours (inventory, assessments, monitoring) |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 hours | W2, W4, W7, W9: 4 to 5 hours (visual inspection inventory, assessment, lifecycle, oversight) |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 to 3 hours | W8, W11, W12: 4 to 5 hours (evidence design, evidence review, walkthrough) |

How the internal auditors participate is a Week 1 decision. If they help build controls, that may affect how independently they can later audit them, so the Client may prefer to limit them to evidence design and review.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** confirm scope, the team, risks to delivery and the second production workflow.
- **Week 6:** review spine status, the artifact register, blockers and any scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** attest to the minimum viable AIMS against the six elements, review the evidence sample and agree on a 12-month operating plan.

Steering group membership is Unknown and will be proposed in the Week 1 mobilization brief.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format.** The program runs for 12 weeks, each with one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions. Session times will be set once participant locations and time zones are confirmed. These are currently Unknown.

**Start date.** To be agreed. As an illustration, a start in the first week of January 2027 would place Week 12 in late March 2027, subject to holidays and scheduling. That would be before Q2 2027.

**Price.** US$60,000. This sits within the stated approved ceiling of US$80,000. The Client's fiscal year end is Unknown, so please confirm that the approved budget remains available for a program that starts after your 15 December 2026 decision. Invoicing schedule and contract terms are to be agreed (confirm with external counsel).

## 8. Next Step

To support a decision by 15 December 2026, we propose a 45-minute scoping call with you to confirm:

1. The target start date and the Client's fiscal year end.
2. Candidates for the second governed workflow in production use.
3. The ISMS and QMS artifacts the AIMS should attach to.
4. The works council consultation timeline as it relates to visual inspection.
5. The internal auditors' role.
6. Steering group membership.

On confirmation, we will issue the Week 1 mobilization brief and the agreement for signature.

**Matters to confirm with external counsel:** EU AI Act classification of each system, works council consultation requirements, GDPR and data residency obligations and the program agreement.
